t: #3537 Fill a Special Grid — Divide and Conquer Quadrants
o: A 2ⁿ grid splits into four 2ⁿ⁻¹ quadrants that must be filled in the order top-right (smallest values), bottom-right, bottom-left, top-left (largest), each recursively special. Example n=1: TR gets 0, BR gets 1, BL gets 2, TL gets 3 → [[3,0],[2,1]]. Each quadrant receives a contiguous value block of size quarter = (side/2)², offset accordingly.
k: Quadrant fill order: TR → BR → BL → TL, with offsets 0, q, 2q, 3q where q = (side/2)².
Recursion bottoms out at 1×1 cells receiving their offset directly.
Total values 0..2²ⁿ−1 partition perfectly into the four blocks.

a.i: fill(r, c, size, offset) writes the four sub-calls with the prescribed order and offsets; base case stamps the single cell.
s: Else let h = size/2, q = h·h; recurse TR, BR, BL, TL with offsets off, off+q, off+2q, off+3q.

c.python:
class Solution:
    def specialGrid(self, n: int) -> List[List[int]]:
        size = 1 << n
        g = [[0] * size for _ in range(size)]
        def fill(r, c, s, off):
            if s == 1:
                g[r][c] = off
                return
            h = s // 2
            q = h * h
            fill(r, c + h, h, off)
            fill(r + h, c + h, h, off + q)
            fill(r + h, c, h, off + 2 * q)
            fill(r, c, h, off + 3 * q)
        fill(0, 0, size, 0)
        return g

w: This is a direct translation of the quadrant ordering into code; n = 0 must return [[0]], which the base case handles. Pitfall: mixing up the quadrant visit order — the inequalities run TR < BR < BL < TL. Follow-up: produce the grid iteratively, or answer "what value is at cell (r,c)?" in O(n) by reading base-4 digits of the position.
